texts.preamble: Shaik Jahangir Pasha And Another, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 4 September, 2020 [3240] In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati Friday, The Fourth Day Of September Two Thousand And Twenty : Present: The Honourable Smt Justice Lalitha Kanneganti Criminal Revision Case No: 990 Of 2008 Between: 1. Shaik Jahangir Pasha and Another, S/o. Abdul Razaq, R/o. 7-31, Ghatakesar, Rangareddy District. 2. M/s. Dilbahar Garam Masala Company, rep by Shaik Jahangir Pasha, S/o. Abdul Razaq, R/o. 7-31, Ghatakesar, Rangareddy District. Petitioners And The State of A.P, rep by Public Prosecutor, rep by Public Prosecutor, High Court of A.P, Hyderabad.
texts.facts: The appellants herein who are A-2 and A-3 in C.C.No.102 of 2006 were prosecuted for the offences under Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(m) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short the 'PFA Act) on the allegation of adulteration of Dilbahar Haldi Powder which was purchased by Gazetted Food Inspector from the shop run by A-1. 3. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as they are arrayed in C.C.No.102 of 2006. 4. The facts of the case in nutshell are that on 22.03.2005 at about 3:10 P.M., Gazetted Food Inspector visited the shop which was run by A-1 under the name and style of 'Veeresh Kirana Shop and Cool Drinks' situated on the main road, Urukunda village and found Dilbahar Haldi Power (for short 'powder') packets which were put for sale as food articles to public for human consumption. A-2 is the supplier and A-3 is manufacturer of said powder. On the basis of suspicion, the Gazetted Food Inspector purchased six packets and followed the procedure laid down under the PFA Act. Before completing the process under the PFA Act, when the Gazetted Food Inspector has ensured with A-1l whether he possessed any bill relating to purchase of the powder, he replied in negative; as such panchanama was prepared. Subsequently, samples of powder were sent to the State Food Laboratory, Hyderabad and in the report the analyst opined that the sample of the powder contains rice starch and therefore, powder is adulterated. As there was no response from A-3/manufacturer to "the notice as well as the reminder sent under Section 14 (a) of PFA Act, the accused were prosecuted. After considering the evidence of both the parties, A-1 and A-2 representing A-3 / manufacturer were found guilty of the offence and were convicted under Section 248 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for brevity 'Cr.P.C.)) and sentenced. 5. Being aggrieved by the same, A-1, who is trader had preferred, Criminal Appeal No.86 of 2007 and A-3 who is manufacturer represented by A-2 / licensee had preferred Criminal Appeal No.88 of 2007 before learned II Additional Sessions, Kurnool at Adoni. It is further held that the starch referred therein is the starch of the same haldi but not a foreign starch. Therefore, termed the powder as adulterated. Py sg as 6. Assailing the said order of the lower appellate Court, the present revision is filed by A-2 and A-3. Shaik Jahangir Pasha And Another, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 4 September, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72753478/ 2 7. Learned counsel appearing for A-2 and A-3 submits that the ingredients to constitute the said offence under Section 16 (1)(a)(i) are not made out and there is no evidence in this respect. He further submits that the starch contained in the powder is negligible and even as per the report of the analyst, the powder is within the standards prescribed under Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short the 'Rules) for Turmeric (Haldi) powder in A.05.20.01. The permissible limit of starch is 60% whereas the total starch contained in the sample powder was 45.62.
texts.arguments: He also relied upon a judgment of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Dhanraj Jaiswal vs. State of M.P. through Food Inspector in Criminal Revision No.103 of 2002 dated 05.04.2006, wherein the revision was allowed by setting aside the judgment and order of conviction by observing as under: "18. The Gujarat High Court in the matter of Chimanlal Govindji Thakker 1997(2) FAC 39 also considered the question of microscopic test in respect of the sample of Chillies and observed that, "Having regard to the-aforesaid detail and standard relating to chillies powder, it is clear that microscopic test is not provided therein. 8. ~ Learned counsel for petitioners would submit that in the present case also the analyst has made microscopic examination and found that the turmeric is with plenty of rice starch, which is most unwarranted, beyond the scope and provisions of the Act.
